title: Finite connected components of geometric coverings over a normal base
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme] which is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Assume that every local ring of $X$ is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $q:Z\to X$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism], with $Z$ not assumed quasi-compact. Suppose that $q$ has the following valuation lifting property. For every valuation ring $R$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, every morphism $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, and every $X$-morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ over the restriction of $b$, there is a unique $X$-morphism $\widetilde a:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Z$ whose restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is $a$. Then every connected component of $|Z|$ (a maximal nonempty connected subset) is open and closed in $|Z|$. With the induced open subscheme structure, each such component $C\subset Z$ has finite etale surjective structural morphism $q|_C:C\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Thus $Z$ is the disjoint union of these connected finite etale $X$-schemes. The scheme $Z$ is allowed to be empty, in which case the indexing set of components is empty; the indexing set need not be finite in general.

source.place: Definition 7.3.1(3), p. 66; proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71, connected geometric coverings are finite etale. Normality supplies geometric unibranchness by literature/stacks-project/properties.tex Tag 0BQ3, lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch. The open-and-closed component decomposition is the first paragraph of that proof; surjectivity follows from the nonempty open and closed image of a finite etale component over connected X.

proof.text: If $Z$ is empty, the conclusion is vacuous. Otherwise apply [lem-a1-normal-etale-components-clopen]. The local normality hypothesis on $X$ gives geometric unibranchness by Tag 0BQ3, etaleness makes $Z$ locally topologically Noetherian, and the cited component lemma therefore makes every connected component $C$ of $Z$ open and closed and irreducible. The induced open-and-closed subscheme structure on $C$ is consequently defined.

source.place: proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71, first paragraph

proof.text: Fix a connected component $C$ of $|Z|$; by step 1 it is open in $|Z|$, and we give it its induced open subscheme structure. The base $X$ is connected, quasi-compact, locally Noetherian with integrally closed local domains, $q$ is etale, and $q$ has the unique valuation lifting property, which are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-a1-geometric-cover-component-qc-proper] for the open connected component $C$. It gives that $q|_C$ is quasi-compact and proper and that $q^{-1}(\{x\})\cap C$ is finite for every $x\in X$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71, generic-fibre and Noetherian-induction paragraphs

proof.text: The base $X$ is locally Noetherian, so [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] applies to $q|_C$: properness and finite fibres imply that $q|_C$ is finite. Since $q$ is etale and $C\hookrightarrow Z$ is open, the restriction is etale; hence $q|_C$ is finite etale.

source.place: Tag 02OG, Lemma coherent-lemma-characterize-finite; finite iff proper with finite fibres

proof.text: Each connected component $C$ is nonempty by definition. The etale image lemma [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] makes the image of $q|_C$ open, while [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] makes it closed because $q|_C$ is finite. Thus the image is nonempty and clopen in connected $X$, so it is all of $X$ and $q|_C$ is surjective.

source.place: Tags 02J3 and 04D1/02GW; nonempty clopen image in connected base

proof.text: The connected components are pairwise disjoint and cover $|Z|$ by their maximality. Because each is open and closed, their induced open subschemes glue to a disjoint union decomposition of $Z$, and the empty scheme has the empty indexing family. The indexing family can be infinite because no global quasi-compactness of $Z$ was assumed.

split_report.summary: Split the geometric-cover component argument into two substantive statement-only children: clopen irreducible components of an etale scheme over a normal locally Noetherian base, and quasi-compactness, properness and finite fibres of an open connected component under the valuation lifting property. The item proof then applies these children, the existing proper-with-finite-fibres characterization of finite morphisms, the existing open-image (etale) and closed-image (finite) nodes for surjectivity, and an explicit disjoint-union argument; the statement is unchanged.

The item statement is unchanged and correct. I tested the empty Z, infinitely many components, and an open immersion that fails the lifting property. Steps 1-5 check out: step 3 uses Tag 02OG via thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres, which I accept as a generic tool use. Step 4 uses the etale open-image and finite closed-image Mathlib leaves. Step 5 is genuinely elementary. Both children are true. For the clopen child: Z is locally Noetherian and normal, so it is geometrically unibranch and its components are clopen. For the qc-proper child: C is integral and separated; ZMT gives an open immersion into the normalization of X in kappa(xi); existence of lifts makes it surjective, so C is finite. Neither child is a duplicate: lem-fin-etale-normal-components and lem-trf-* need a Noetherian or affine source. Neither restates the item, and there is no cycle. Batch-5 check: def-trf-valuation-ring is a pure general definition that the item's base statement already cited. It is neither assumption nor part of their proofs, so it is accepted. Fixes: (1) clopen child: cite def-sc-ring-strict-henselization and def-weil-irreducible-components, define locally topologically Noetherian and connected component inline. (2) qc-proper child: it presupposed C open, so C is now assumed to be an open connected component (step 1 provides that); cite def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism and pqf-def-quasifinite; item step 2 text adjusted.
